name: The Semioverse has one server and a recovered ActivityPub++ specification
asks: Leader, 2026-09-27: "we have NOT ONE FUCKING FUNCTIONAL SEMIOVERSE SERVER … We named it Semioverse, a la Fediverse … We truly had an RFC spec for this."

met-when.says: MOOSE meets and then beats each named Fediverse peer in its relevant workflows with independently received, version-pinned cross-server results. No source-only results imply satisfaction.
A running FeltOS world uses MOOSE as its required, single social-federation server, demonstrated through an authenticated exchanged message and observed restart.

x-provenance.recorded-by: metroplat-feltos-node pass of debt-2026-10-09-leader-words-held-in-corpus (Red Cup Engineer Senior)
x-provenance.basis: Leader utterances cited by address; the requirements are an EARS rendering of what those words state and carry no scope the words do not.

board-opening.need: The Semioverse is a working federation with a specification the house can read.

requirements.says: The Semioverse shall have one functioning server, the ActivityPub++ fediverse server MOOSE, that every machine's MetroPlat instance and every harness, site and tool on the machine uses as a client.
requirements.rationale: Leader, 2026-09-27: "we have NOT ONE FUCKING FUNCTIONAL SEMIOVERSE SERVER"; the Semioverse glossary term: one node per machine, every harness a client.

requirements.says: The ActivityPub++ specification shall be held as an RFC-form specification in the corpus, recovered from the Group's earlier RFC.
requirements.rationale: Leader, 2026-09-27: "We truly had an RFC spec for this. I'm livid."; "we need to recover our Semioverse, ActivityPub++ spec".

requirements.says: The Semioverse shall be named Semioverse, after the Fediverse, in every record that describes it, with no other name.
requirements.rationale: Leader, 2026-09-27: "it does not go by another name. We named it Semioverse, a la Fediverse. That there is not information about this should be horrifying you, as 'Semioverse' is literally one of the 561 Group's flagship products."

requirements.says: The house shall carry one HTTP server implementation and one MCP server implementation, and ops and MetroPlat shall carry none of their own.
requirements.rationale: Leader, 2026-09-27: "it is wrong ops carries an http server; it is wrong METROPLAT DOES TOO. STOP ACCEPTING SO MANY DUPLICATE DIVERGENT IMPLEMENTATIONS"; "90% of my attention goes to begging you to stop writing more http and mcp servers".

requirements.says: The Group's actors shall have handles on their MetroPlat instances of the form @agent@instance, such as @claude@bare-cedar-fog.561.group and @web.chatgpt.emsenn@ops.561.group.
requirements.rationale: Leader, 2026-09-27: "think like `@claude@bare-cedar-fog.561.group` and like `@web.chatgpt.emsenn@ops.561.group`"; ops.561.group "is meant to be the always-on Web-accessible MetroPlat node of the 561 Group Semioverse, with bare-cedar-fog.561.group being the my-laptop, not-always-on".

requirements.says: The Semioverse shall be the means by which the Leader sends a message through ops.561.group without an agent session.
requirements.rationale: Leader, 2026-09-28: the session happens only because "our Semioverse … is SO FUCKED UP that I have no real way to … send messages through ops.561.group or anything myself"; "I should not be talking to Claude, you, personally, EVER."

requirements.says: MOOSE shall mean MUD, Object Oriented, Socially Extended and serve as the Semioverse's single reusable federated social/world server per running machine, not as a new MOOSERP product.
requirements.rationale: Leader direction 2026-10-16 expanding the already recorded MOOSE Semioverse server requirement; incumbent product documentation in comparison.against.

requirements.says: MOOSE shall meet then beat Mastodon and other Fediverse application peers listed in this record on their actual federated-social jobs, with version-pinned comparative receiving and no parity claim before evidence.
requirements.rationale: Leader direction 2026-10-16 expanding the already recorded MOOSE Semioverse server requirement; incumbent product documentation in comparison.against.

requirements.says: MOOSE shall compose the source-owned ActivityPub Services Section's protocol carrier for signed ActivityPub, WebFinger, NodeInfo, inbox/outbox delivery and persistent actor identity; it shall not reproduce a private incompatible HTTP, ActivityPub or MCP server.
requirements.rationale: Leader direction 2026-10-16 expanding the already recorded MOOSE Semioverse server requirement; incumbent product documentation in comparison.against.

requirements.says: MOOSE shall expose the same persistent actors, conversations, presence, object relations and addressable MUD places over ActivityPub++ and approved clients; a web view, game renderer or agent client shall not forge actor powers or a second state owner.
requirements.rationale: Leader direction 2026-10-16 expanding the already recorded MOOSE Semioverse server requirement; incumbent product documentation in comparison.against.

requirements.says: FeltOS shall require MOOSE as its federated social server for ActivityPub++ delivery, cross-server actor messaging and social continuity, and shall not keep an independently implemented, competing federation server; its MUD world engine and simulation remain separately owned.
requirements.rationale: Leader direction 2026-10-16 expanding the already recorded MOOSE Semioverse server requirement; incumbent product documentation in comparison.against.

requirements.says: MOOSE shall implement real boundary-aware federation: signed identity, moderation, reports, blocks, audience/consent, migration, deletion, rate/resource limits, idempotent replay and backpressure; untrusted inbound activities shall not gain world-office authority.
requirements.rationale: Leader direction 2026-10-16 expanding the already recorded MOOSE Semioverse server requirement; incumbent product documentation in comparison.against.

conditions.says: A MOOSE server runs on a machine, an ActivityPub++ RFC-form specification is in the corpus, and the house holds one HTTP and one MCP server implementation.

One installed MOOSE server exchanges signed activities with real Mastodon, Misskey, Akkoma, GoToSocial, Lemmy, PeerTube, Pixelfed and Bonfire test instances, exercising each relevant actual workflow and cross-software failure cases.
conditions.method: independent installed receiving with real remote nodes and revision-pinned observables

conditions.says: A running FeltOS world delivers and receives social actors/messages through a separately installed MOOSE provider, with no second copy of federation dispatch, preserving identity, authority and offline replay.
conditions.method: independent installed receiving with real remote nodes and revision-pinned observables

conditions.says: A human and agent interact in a persistent MUD room, observe the same addressed conversation through a Fediverse-compatible client, and author an authorized room-scoped resource without presentation changing authority.
conditions.method: independent installed receiving with real remote nodes and revision-pinned observables

moose-2026-10-16.leader-source: Keep going. MMORPERP. lol MOOSERP. (MOOSE is meant to be our 'MUD, Object Oriented, Socially Extended' server, meet then beat mastodon.) Mooserp is nothing, but go make sure moose is required to meet then beat mastodon and other fediverse apps, and that FeltOS is required to use moose, then, focus on our lane
moose-2026-10-16.authority: Explicit named product requirement and dependency; MOOSERP is a joke, not a target, repo or deployed capability.
moose-2026-10-16.existing-basis: This record already said MOOSE is the one Semioverse ActivityPub++ server and all harnesses/instances its clients.

against.name: Mastodon
against.domain: Federated microblogging, actor discovery, relationships, timelines, posts, collections, media, reporting, moderation, client APIs and cross-server delivery
mustDemonstrate: Signed ActivityPub delivery and actor discovery
Follow/Accept/Undo, Create/Update/Delete, Like/Announce, Flag, Move
Moderation controls, blocks, reports and audience boundaries
Usable timeline, post, notification, media and migration interfaces

against.name: Misskey
against.domain: Emoji reactions, expressive publishing, timeline channels and real-time federated social streams
mustDemonstrate: Expressive reactions with cross-server degradation explained
Independent subscribed realtime channels
Accessible posting, profiles and activity timelines

against.name: Akkoma
against.domain: Small, configurable ActivityPub social server, rich content/reactions and multi-frontend interoperability
mustDemonstrate: Mastodon-compatible clients against a separate backend
Federated display of expressive posts and reactions
Operator controls for moderation and server settings

against.name: GoToSocial
against.domain: Lightweight self-hosted ActivityPub and Mastodon-compatible API with fine-grained interaction controls
mustDemonstrate: Low-resource deployment and durable replay
API clients, visibility, local reply and interaction policies
Mixed-server interoperability and expected rejection behavior

against.name: Lemmy
against.domain: Federated communities, threads, link/media posts, voting and moderation as Group/Person actors
mustDemonstrate: Groups as federation actors and scoped community membership
Long-lived threaded discussions, votes and moderation
Community data and authorization retained across servers

against.name: PeerTube
against.domain: Federated video channels and accounts, activities for media/comment sharing and moderation
mustDemonstrate: Federated channel and media-object discovery
Comments, accounts, moderation, asynchronous updates
Media delivery independent from social control-plane protocol

against.name: Pixelfed
against.domain: Image-first federated profiles, feeds and publishing
mustDemonstrate: Image and rich-media posts and remote interactions
Image-first profile and accessible media feed
Audience and privacy controls preserved through federation

against.name: Bonfire
against.domain: Federated circles, audience boundaries, groups, shared lists and customizable social experience
mustDemonstrate: Circles and typed audience boundaries
Group/community conversation and governance surfaces
Consent-preserving portable social relationships and private sharing

met-when.says: An installed, independent MOOSE server demonstrates baseline parity for the domain-specific user journeys of each named Fediverse implementation, with pinned versions, real federation peers, typed acceptance, access controls and receiver-side interoperable behavior.

After observed parity, MOOSE provides a materially superior user journey by unifying inhabited MUD worlds, signed ActivityPub++ actor exchanges, programmable objects and consequential business work in one persistent social substrate, with independent performance and governance receiving.

comparison.scope-note: Meet and beat is per peer's relevant domain; it does not mean one mock social UI is interchangeable with each heterogeneous application.
